_comment: Data centers only. Split out from elsa_yt because on their own they sweep
all 127 Oklahoma places in under two weeks instead of sixteen, and because
a data center is demand rather than generation — a different thing to be
asking about even when the fight looks the same.
The codebook is identical to the one in elsa_yt on purpose. Both exports
then carry the same columns, so the two can be stacked in a spreadsheet
and compared directly. Keep them in sync.
_home_comment: Used to fill in the home state when a video names no state at all.
Local stations rarely say 'Oklahoma' in a title, so a KOCO story about
Luther or a Stitt interview otherwise has no state and drops out of an
Oklahoma filter. Nothing is filled in when another state is named, and
local_because records which signal was used.
home_stations      call letters and brand names, matched in the channel
home_channel_words place words, matched in the channel name only
ambiguous_towns    towns on the cities list that are common place names
elsewhere; on their own they do not set the state

_scoring_comment: A video must clear two separate tests, not one combined score.
1. Subject. A topic phrase has to appear in the title or description.
2. Local signal. It has to be tied to somewhere in the United States:

channels through. Points now only order the results; the two tests
_limits_comment: search.list bills to its own bucket of roughly 100 calls a day, so
searches_per_run is the thing to watch. commentThreads costs one unit
per page of 100 from the 10,000-unit pool and is effectively free.
YouTube's developer policies require stored API data to be deleted or
refreshed within 30 calendar days. Every run refreshes every tracked
video. When one drops out, its comment text goes and the link and
_topics_comment: Two tiers, because 77 counties times seven technologies is 539 searches and
statewide runs every week for every technology, so anything that makes the
Oklahoma news is caught within a week.
county_template is rotated: each run takes the next county_block pairs of
county and technology and works through them, picking up where it left off.
A full cycle takes a few months and runs in the background.
Set county_template to null for a topic with too little volume to be worth
_cities_comment: Oklahoma counties mostly do not zone; municipalities do. A data center or
battery site near a town is decided by a city council, and the coverage is
titled 'Norman city council', never 'Cleveland County'. So cities are
searched alongside counties and go into the same rotation.
Cities also count as a local signal in their own right, so a clip about
Yukon from a channel with no call letters is still recognized as local.
